The Director-General of the Commission, Hon. Bukola Olopade, said the initiative was designed to address decades of infrastructure deficits that have hindered athlete development, weakened Nigeria’s international competitiveness and limited the country’s capacity to host major sporting events.
In a statement signed by his Special Adviser on Media, Kola Daniel, on Saturday, Olopade said several projects were either ongoing or at the approval stage as the Commission intensified efforts to reposition sports as a contributor to economic growth.
Among the major projects is the rehabilitation of the historic Mudashiru Lawal Stadium in Abeokuta, Ogun State, estimated at ₦2.5 billion.
The project includes the installation of new tartan tracks and rehabilitation of existing facilities to bring the stadium up to modern sporting standards.
In Enugu State, the Commission is supporting the construction of an Olympic-size swimming pool, alongside upgrades to the indoor sports hall and rehabilitation of athletes’ hostels to strengthen aquatic sports and improve the state’s capacity to host major competitions.
However, one of the most extensive interventions is the planned comprehensive redevelopment of the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja.
According to the Commission, the Federal Government has approved a complete overhaul of the stadium’s main pitch and tartan tracks, as well as improvements to the dressing rooms, media centre, VIP seating, corporate suites, public address systems, security facilities and roof membrane.
The project will also include internationally compliant floodlighting, electronic advertising boards, Video Assistant Referee (VAR) technology and a protective pitch cover to allow the stadium to host concerts and other commercial events without damaging the playing surface.
Beyond the main stadium, approvals have been granted for a High Performance Centre, the conversion of the existing 200-bed athletes’ hostel into a modern hotel, rehabilitation of the Package B swimming pool and construction of two additional training pitches.
The proposed High Performance Centre will provide facilities for elite athlete preparation, sports science, performance monitoring and other specialised support services.
The Commission’s infrastructure programme also extends to grassroots sports, with approvals secured for sports centres in 15 tertiary institutions across the country’s six geopolitical zones.
Another 20 mini sports centres and stadiums are planned for communities nationwide to expand access to sporting facilities, encourage youth participation and strengthen talent identification.
Other projects include the ongoing redevelopment of Ahmadu Bello Stadium in Kaduna through a partnership with the Kaduna State Government, with completion expected in 2027.
The construction of Bichi Stadium in Kano is also being undertaken through collaboration between the Commission and the National Assembly.
The NSC further disclosed that plans were at an advanced stage for the redevelopment of the National Stadium in Lagos through government and private-sector investment, as well as the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium in Ibadan through a partnership with the Oyo State Government.
Olopade said the Commission’s vision went beyond building and renovating sporting facilities, stressing the need to make infrastructure commercially viable and sustainable.
He identified the National Sports Infrastructure Development Bond, approved by President Bola Tinubu, as a key funding mechanism for the rehabilitation, redevelopment and maintenance of critical sports facilities across the country.
The initiative is aligned with the Renewed Hope Initiative for Nigeria Sports Economy (RHINSE), through which the Federal Government seeks to position sports as a driver of economic growth, job creation, youth empowerment and national development.
Under the leadership of NSC Chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, and Olopade, the Commission said it was pursuing an integrated sports development model in which modern infrastructure would support talent discovery, elite performance, grassroots participation, sports tourism and private-sector investment.
The Commission maintained that the nationwide projects would provide opportunities for athletes, young people and businesses while strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to compete internationally and host major sporting events.
